ITEM WORDING + INSTRUCTIONS: S1 Questionnaire, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0274964.s002 (DOCX, sha256 391ac371865a9d7872d6152f0d2ac813986fae7139f9ae358fa85f7e806549b3), which prints all 26 MTP-Q items as a numbered list 1-26 and a construct table (TASK = 1+6+11+16+21+26; AUTHORITY = 2+7+12+17+22; RECOGNITION = 5+8+13+18+23; GROUPING = 4+9+14+19+24; EVALUATION = 3+10+15+20+25). RESPONSE DATA / CODES: S1 Dataset, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0274964.s001 (SPSS .sav, sha256 32cecfd721576bd36c5d4717ab3e6d953a8c3ef0908fb3ba58d30ab9363d9d36). note: PASS with caveats (batch_220). GATE: validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets exactly (26 items Task_1..Task_6, Authority_1..5, Recognition_1..5, Grouping_1..5, Evaluation_1..5; resp set 1-5); 130 rows = 26 items x 5 levels. Retry test: not applicable, this is a write. (1) CODE DERIVATION. data/weeldenburg_2022_target_pe.py melts the S1 Dataset's own columns by PREFIX MATCH on 'Task_','Authority_','Recognition_','Grouping_','Evaluation_' -- the IRW item code IS the .sav column name, with no positional assignment and no rename. But the source grants no exemption on content: the .sav's variable labels for those 26 columns are bare internal codes ('TA_1','AU_1','RE_1','GR_1','EV_1', ...) carrying no item text, and the item columns have NO value labels at all (pyreadstat reports value labels only for Geslacht, Niveau, TSC_2, TSC_3 and filter_$). So the file ties code to code, not code to words; mapping_basis is paper_order, not data_labels. (2) ITEM TEXT comes from S1 Questionnaire, transcribed verbatim from its DOCX table via python-docx (no manual retyping), including the source's curly apostrophes and its 'It doesn't matter...' / '(playing)rules' spacing. Nothing was normalised. instructions is the supplement's own introduction paragraph with the literal label 'Introduction: ' stripped; nothing else altered. (3) THE MAPPING, and what is inferred. S1 Questionnaire numbers the items 1-26 and assigns them to constructs, but does not print the codes the .sav uses. Construct membership is therefore explicit; the ordinal suffix within a construct is INFERRED as the ascending questionnaire number (Authority_1 = Nr 2, Authority_2 = Nr 7, ... Authority_5 = Nr 22). The questionnaire's own numbering makes that the only coherent reading: the 26 items are block-interleaved five at a time -- Nr 1-5 is one item of each construct, Nr 6-10 the next, and so on, with Task taking the extra Nr 26 -- so item k of every construct sits in block k. (4) VERIFICATION: PARTIAL, routes 3 and 8, re-runnable as verify_weeldenburg_2022_targetmtpq.R (VERDICT: PASS). Each prefix block reproduces the paper's Table 1 row for the construct it names, to every printed digit: Task 3.557/0.701/alpha 0.784 vs 3.56/.70/.79, Authority 3.000/0.852/0.793 vs 3.00/.85/.79, Recognition 3.657/0.788/0.850 vs 3.66/.79/.85, Grouping 3.368/0.805/0.800 vs 3.37/.80/.80, Evaluation 3.443/0.787/0.818 vs 3.44/.79/.82 (largest deviation 0.0059). All five published means are distinct, so no block-level permutation of the text is possible. Two within-block positions are additionally pinned by content signature: the paper says three items were moved to another construct after the EFA, and two Authority items name another construct's content -- Nr 7 is about evaluation/assessment activities and Nr 22 about the grouping process. Of the five Authority items, Authority_2 (claimed Nr 7) is the ONLY one whose strongest rival-block correlation is Evaluation (0.43 vs Task 0.27, Recognition 0.30, Grouping 0.39) and Authority_5 (claimed Nr 22) the ONLY one whose strongest is Grouping (0.49 vs 0.35/0.41/0.42) -- exactly as the shipped assignment predicts. NOT ESTABLISHED: the position of Authority_1/_3/_4 inside their block, or of any Task_*, Recognition_*, Grouping_* or Evaluation_* item; a permutation inside a block changes none of these numbers. Hence PARTIAL. (5) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK. The 3,150 respondents are Dutch secondary-school students (vmbo/havo/vwo tracks) and the administration was in Dutch -- the paper never states this in words, but the .sav's own covariate names and value labels are Dutch (Leraar, Geslacht, Leeftijd, Niveau; 1=jongen/2=meisje; vmbo/havo/vwo). The administered Dutch wording is NOT recoverable in scope: the deposit is the .sav (English-coded variable labels only, zero Dutch item text), and the paper's only other supplement, S2 (doi:...s003), is the peer-review rebuttal letter, not an instrument. So the 2026-09-01 fallback applies -- the authors' own English in S1 Questionnaire ships in the base fields, the _translated columns stay empty, language=Dutch is the signal, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. No English was produced by this project, so nothing is owed under the machine_translation rule. (6) OPTION TEXT: only the two endpoints ship. S1 Questionnaire states 'Each item is responded to on a 5-point Likert-type scale (1 = strongly disagree; 5 = strongly agree)' and the paper repeats exactly those endpoints; resp 2, 3 and 4 are BLANK because the source labels no middle anchors and a scale point was not padded with its own number. All five levels are used by every item (each item has n=3150 with 5 distinct levels, per irw_table_sets per-item output), so the coverage is complete. (7) STEP 3b, instrument identity checked rather than assumed. The dictionary calls this the 26-item MTP-Q and the live data is 26 items on 1-5 with n=3150 per item, no missing. The same .sav also holds the study's OTHER instrument, the 12-item BRPEQ (IntrinsicMot/IdentifiedReg/IntrojectedReg/ExternalReg/Amotivation), which is the separate IRW table weeldenburg_2022_brpeq_motivation and is NOT touched here; the 6/5/5/5/5 split, the per-construct reproduction of Table 1 above, and the .sav's own aggregate columns (TASK_mean/AUTH_mean/RECOG_mean/GROU_mean/EVAL_mean each equal the mean of the corresponding block to 0.00e+00) confirm the table is the MTP-Q. (8) RIGHTS: no block. The MTP-Q was newly constructed BY THE AUTHORS OF THIS STUDY ('The initial items were generated by the authors of this study') and published by them in the CC BY 4.0 article's own supplement, so the originator and the open publisher are the same party; there is no upstream instrument whose page could govern. instrument_rights_register.csv has no MTP-Q row and none was added (a round may write only block rows). No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause appears in the article, the supplement or anywhere the authors publish the instrument -- silence is permission. (9) section_id is the trivial weeldenburg_2022_targetmtpq_1 (no testlets or passages); section_prompt, correct_response and all four _translated columns blank throughout.
